drivingQuestion: What is the reason a stain on the tip of her big toe renders her impure?
outcomeNote: The question stands at the unit's end; answered in niddah.sugya274 (the toe is different, it lies under her while walking).

segments.he: עַל עֲקֵבָהּ וְעַל רֹאשׁ גּוּדָלָהּ טְמֵאָה וְכוּ׳. בִּשְׁלָמָא עֲקֵבָהּ, עֲבִיד דְּנָגַע בְּאוֹתוֹ מָקוֹם, אֶלָּא רֹאשׁ גּוּדָלָהּ מַאי טַעְמָא? וְכִי תֵּימָא זִימְנִין דְּנָגַע בַּעֲקֵבָהּ, וּמִי מְחַזְּקִינַן טוּמְאָה מִמָּקוֹם לְמָקוֹם?
segments.en: § The mishna teaches: If a stain was discovered on her heel or on the tip of her large «toe,» although it is not adjacent to her vagina «she is ritually impure,» as blood from the uterus could have reached there. The Gemara comments: «Granted,» when blood is found on «her heel» she is impure, as «it is wont to touch that place,» her vagina, when she kneels. «But» if the blood is discovered «on the tip of her large toe, what is the reason» she is thereby rendered impure? «And if you would say» the reason is that «sometimes» the tip of one large toe might «touch her heel,» i.e., the heel of the other foot, «do we presume» that «ritual impurity» travels «from place to place?» Since that is not presumed, the stain on the large toe of one foot cannot be presumed to come from the heel of the other foot.
